title: Forge provider wait v1 (an additive payload extension at event_schema 1)
description: Decision 0103 rulings 2(a) and 4(a): the optional, absent-by-default payload fields that record a provider's rate-limit cool-down and the probe that ends it. `effect/failed.waits` (and, from decision 0103 slice 4c2, `effect/indeterminate.waits`) is one entry per refused site: the journal tag (absent for an inline seat), the provider and route the driver already resolved, the provider's bounded words, its retry-after when given, the computed `until`, and the round of the effect's episode. `effect/started.probe` is the one answer a dedicated one-turn probe gave before its retry, with the site, provider, route and when it answered. Both fields are optional and absent by default, are published as a numbered extension at event_schema 1 under the amended rule in contracts/README.md, and are never read by `fold`: the engine reads them from the effect's own events and `RunState` gains nothing. A present entry that cannot be read refuses by name, never as absent.

waits.description: Present on a terminal `effect/failed`, and (slice 4c2) on `effect/indeterminate`, only when at least one site's typed rate-limit refusal recorded a wait. One entry per refused site; a single seat carries exactly one.

probe.description: Present on the retry's `effect/started` only after a dedicated probe answered, so the wait's end has a record. A probe that ended without an answer writes none.

site.description: The invocation-site tag the journal already uses for checkpoints and provenance: '<member>' for a panel member, '<step>' for a sequence step, '<step>:<member>' for a member inside a step panel. Absent for an inline seat, which has no tag.

provider.description: The provider name the adapter's declaration uses (claude, lanetally, codex, dsh, exec, ...), filled from the adapter and never parsed from prose.

route.description: The route the driver serves the pinned model on: the concrete model id's prefix before its first `/` (decision 0036 ruling 2), from the one predicate the producer and this pattern share. A route that could not be resolved parks naming it and records no wait: a null route would be a provider-wide hold over unrelated routes.

words.description: The provider's bounded evidence line, in its own words. One line, clamped, never a transcript.

retry_after_seconds.description: The provider's own retry-after in whole seconds, when it gave one. It is the wait as given and is never lengthened; a later round doubles only the route's declared default.

until.description: The computed end of this round's wait: now plus the provider's retry-after, else the route's default doubled for each earlier round of the same effect and site. A resume reads it and waits the remainder.

rounds.description: Which round of this effect's and site's episode this wait is: one for the first refusal, two for the next. It is the exponent the route's default doubles by.

site.description: The invocation-site tag the probe asked, tagged as `waits.site` is. Absent for an inline seat.

provider.description: The provider the probe asked, as the wait entry names it.

route.description: The cooled route the probe asked, as the wait entry names it.

answered_at.description: When the probe's first model-output answer arrived. A session start, `accepted`, a spawn, a hang, a deadline or an error is not an answer and records none.
